docs.title: Get help with Adaptify
docs.text:
Choose Contact Adaptify support at the bottom of any page. TODO verify the support channel and its URL.

To get help faster, include the page you were on, what you were trying to do and what you saw.

docs.title: Report a problem with the docs
docs.text:
1. Go to the page with the problem.
  2. At the bottom of the page, choose Report a problem with this page. It opens a pre-filled issue.
  3. Describe what's wrong, where on the page, and what you expected.

docs.title: Tell us if a page helped
docs.text: At the bottom of any page, answer Was this page helpful? with Yes or No. Each opens a short pre-filled issue where you can add details.

docs.title: Workbench overview
docs.text: Project Workbench is a collaborative environment for building new products and updating existing products. Open it from Workbench in the left navigation.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• The page header: "Collaborative workspace to plan, execute, and track product changes from idea through approval, filing, and implementation."
  • Cards for the kinds of work:
  • Form updates: modify policy forms and endorsements.
  • Rate updates: adjust rating factors and structures.
  • Rules updates: modify underwriting rules.
  • New product: create a new insurance product.

TODO verify what each card opens. - Project portfolio: your projects, with a count. - Filter them with Type. - Switch between list and grid views. - Turn on Show Archived Projects Only to see archived projects. TODO verify which completed projects appear there. - + New project: at the top right of the Project portfolio. See Create a project.

docs.title: Inside a project
docs.text:
A project page shows a phase stepper, for example Select, Review, Approve and End, with the person working on each phase. Below it are tabs for the work, such as Forms, Notes, Team and Activity.

A combined project lists its child projects on a Projects tab and shows how many are complete.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Create a project
  • Update forms
  • Update rates

docs.title: Move work through phases
docs.text: Each Workbench project follows a workflow made of phases. When your part is done, you submit the project to the next phase and hand it to the next person.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to Workbench and open the project. If your update covers several types, open the child project you're working on, for example the forms project (see Update forms).
  2. Check the current phase on the project page.
  3. Select Submit. The dialog shows the Current phase and Next phase.
  4. Under Select Assignee, choose the person for the next phase.
  5. If you want a due date, pick it from the calendar. It's optional.
  6. Under Add notes, add notes for the next person, for example "Ready for review."
  7. Select Submit. You see "Successfully submitted!", and the project moves to the next phase.

Moving from Approve to End asks only for notes.

From Review on, the person in that phase can also select Reject.

Tip

Pick dates from the calendar instead of typing them. Wait for the dialog to finish before you move on.

docs.title: Phases by project type
docs.text:
Project type Workflow Phases Forms Product Update Select → Review → Approve → End Rates Rate Update Select → End Rules Rule Update Select → Review → Approve → End

Your organization admin manages these workflows under Workflow management on the Dashboard. TODO verify whether your organization's workflows have the same phases.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: When every child project reaches End, complete the project. See Complete a project.

docs.title: Update forms
docs.text: Use a form project to give one or more forms a new edition. If your project is combined, first open its forms child project from the Projects tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the project. Its Forms tab lists the forms in the project.
  2. Choose Add form. The Add form changes dialog opens.
  3. Under Change type, choose Update form, then choose Next.
  4. Select the forms to update, then choose Next.
  5. Enter the Updated edition, for example 01 27. TODO verify which step asks for it.
  6. Check the Confirm step, then choose Change.

The forms appear on the Forms tab with their new edition. When the work is done, use Submit to move the project to its next phase.

Shared forms

If a form is shared by other products or states, the update starts as a draft. The shared document and its unique key stay unchanged until you publish.

TODO verify: - Inactivate form and Create form: not covered yet - editing a form's content

docs.title: Update rates
docs.text: Use a rate project to give one or more rate files a new edition. If your project is combined, first open its rates child project from the Projects tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the project. Its Rates tab lists the rates in the project.
  2. Choose Add rate. The Add rate changes dialog opens. TODO verify the button label.
  3. Under Change type, choose Update rate, then choose Next.
  4. Select the rates to update, then choose Next.
  5. Enter the Updated edition, for example 01 27. TODO verify which step asks for it.
  6. Check the Confirm step, then confirm the change. TODO verify the button label.

The rates appear on the Rates tab with their new edition. A rate project moves from Select straight to End: when the work is done, use Submit to move it to End.

TODO verify: Inactivate rate isn't covered yet.

docs.title: Update rules
docs.text: A rules project changes the rules of a product that's already published in the Product Vault. You run it in the Project Workbench (the Workbench), like a forms or rates update.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The product is published in each state you want to change. Only published states can be picked. See Review and publish.
  • Have the updated rules manual ready.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to Workbench, select + New project, then choose Product update. See Start a product update.
  2. In Setup, under Project type, choose Rules. Select Next.
  3. In Configuration, choose the product and the states (jurisdictions) to change.
  4. In Finalize, enter a title and description, choose the Rule Update workflow, and pick a due date from the calendar. Select Create. TODO verify the Finalize field labels for a rules project.
  5. In the rules project, add your rule changes. TODO verify the name of the add-rule-changes action and its dialog.
  6. Move the project to End with Submit. The Rule Update workflow goes Select → Review → Approve → End. See Move work through phases.

Uploading a whole manual

A manual you upload in a rules project is added as one rule. It isn't split into separate rules, and a rules project can't copy rules from another state.

docs.title: Reuse rules from another state
docs.text: When you add a state, you can reuse the rules already generated for an earlier state: download the generated rules from that state's earlier project and add them to the new state's rules project. TODO verify these steps. This path hasn't been tested yet.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: When the project reaches End, complete it. See Complete a project.

docs.title: Complete a project: Admitted or Non-admitted
docs.text:
When every child project has reached End, you finish the project with Complete project. The dialog has two tabs. Pick the one that matches how each state is regulated.

Choose When Result Admitted The state needs a filing. One filing per state in Filing Manager. The state gets its new release after the filing is approved and archived. Non-admitted The state doesn't need a filing. A new release in the Product Vault, with no filing.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Every child project is at End. See Move work through phases.
  • For Admitted, your organization's filing owners are set up. TODO verify where they're set up (possibly System Administration → Workflow Definition).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
• Complete as Admitted (create filings)
  • Complete as Non-admitted

docs.title: Complete as Admitted (create filings)
docs.text: Use Admitted for states that need a filing. Adaptify creates one filing for each state in Filing Manager.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to Workbench and open the project. Every child project should be at End.
  2. Select Complete project.
  3. Choose the Admitted tab. The filing owners load for your organization.
  4. For each state, choose the Approval Type (Prior approval, File and use or Use and file) and the Owner. The dialog tells you how many filing projects it will create. TODO verify what the per-state Filing field controls.
  5. Review the summary, then confirm. TODO verify the confirm button label.
  6. Open Filing Manager. Each state has its own filing, named after your project and the state, for example "Filing - Personal Auto fall update (Form, Rate) (AL)".

Tip

Pick any dates from the calendar. Don't press Escape inside a date field: it closes the whole dialog, and you start again.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: Each state's filing moves on its own: build the package, file with the state, track objections, record the approval and archive to a new release. The Release to New Release guide walks through every step. For the filing page itself, see Filing Manager overview.

docs.title: Complete as Non-admitted
docs.text: Use Non-admitted for states that don't need a filing, for example when you add a new state to a product. Completing the project creates a release in the Product Vault directly.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to Workbench and open the project. Every child project should be at End.
  2. Select Complete project.
  3. Choose the Non-admitted tab.
  4. Select Add non-admitted and choose the State. Under Release association, choose Create new release or an existing release. For a new state or a new product, the Release version is Baseline. TODO verify how you choose an existing release.
  5. Pick the New business effective date and Renewal effective date from the calendar and enter a Description. Then select Preview and check it: it lists each state, its release and each asset's change.
  6. Select Complete project.
  7. Open Product Vault, then the product and state. The release you created is listed under Release. A new Baseline release is marked Current release, with no Review & publish step.

Tip

Preview works only with dates picked from the calendar, not typed. Don't press Escape inside a date field: it closes the whole dialog.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: Check the new release in the Product Vault. See Understand releases. To add the state's rules, see Update rules.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
In Workbench, choose + New project at the top right of the Project portfolio. A menu opens with two choices, Product update and New product. New product also covers adding a state to an existing product:

Choice Use it to Guide Product update Update forms, rates or rules of a product that's already published in the Vault. Start a product update New product Create a new insurance product. Build a new product in Workbench New product, then New jurisdiction for existing product Add a state to a product that's already in the Vault, starting from another state's forms. Start a project to add a state

docs.title: Start a project to add a state
docs.text:
A New jurisdiction for existing product project adds a state to a product that's already in the Vault. The new state starts from another state's forms. You find it under New product in the New project menu.

Use this when you're expanding into a new state where you don't have the product yet. If you already sell the product in the state but the state was never added in Adaptify, add it with Edit product instead.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: The product is published in the state you'll copy from. See Review and publish.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Workbench, select + New project, then New product.
  2. Product: under Product type, keep New jurisdiction for existing product. It's selected at first.
  3. Project: choose Forms.

  4. Configuration: keep Product Vault as the Product source type. Choose the Source product and the Source jurisdiction whose forms you want to copy. Source jurisdiction lists only states that have a release.

  5. Source: choose the Target jurisdiction (the new state) and the Type of insurance, for example 19.0 Personal Auto. Add a Subtype of insurance if one applies. The Existing product is already filled in.

  6. Finalize: enter the Project title and Project description, choose the Workflow, and pick a Due date from the calendar. Add anyone else under Additional members.

  7. Select Create project. The project opens in the Select phase. The Forms tab lists the source state's forms with the change type Include.

Target jurisdiction lists only states the product doesn't have yet.

Known limitation: forms only

This project copies the source state's forms only. Rates, manuals and supporting materials aren't copied. To add the new state's rules after it's published, see Update rules.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: Review the copied forms, add the new state's own forms and publish the new state. See Copy a state's forms to a new state.

docs.title: Start a product update
docs.text: Start a product update when a published product needs changes to its forms, rates or rules. One project can cover several states.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The product is published in each state you want to change. See Review and publish.
  • Your organization's document storage is set up. Form work needs it. TODO verify who sets it up.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Workbench, choose + New project, then Product update.
  2. Setup: under Project type, choose Forms, Rates or Rules, then choose Next. Choose more than one to create a combined project with a child project for each type.
  3. Configuration: choose the Product and the Jurisdictions, for example Personal Auto and Alabama. Then choose Next.
  4. Finalize: enter the Project title and a short Project description, for example "Personal Auto – Fall 2026 forms and rates update".
  5. Choose the Workflow, for example Product Update, and pick a Due date from the calendar.
  6. You're listed under Default members. Add teammates under Additional members if you need them.
  7. Choose Create.

A single project opens at its first phase, Select. A combined project opens on its Projects tab, listing a child project for each type. Next, add your changes: Update forms or Update rates.

Good to know

  • The states you choose decide which Vault files the update can use. The states that get filed are worked out later from what you change.
  • Keep the description short. Only the first 100 characters are kept.

TODO verify: - whether Finalize also asks for an Owner - the Finalize fields for a combined project, for example a separate workflow per type

docs.title: Build a new product in Workbench
docs.text:
Note

This workflow is still being built, so steps and screens may change.

A New product project takes a brand-new insurance product from idea to build in the Project Workbench (the Workbench). Your team works on it together, phase by phase, like any other project. When you complete it, the product lands in the Product Vault with its first release.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
1. Start a new product project. Choose New product and work through the project wizard.
  2. Add the product's documents: add each form with its file. A project has one type, so rates and rules each need their own project (a Rates or Rules project).
  3. Finish and publish the new product: move the project to End and complete it as Non-admitted. The product gets a Baseline release, marked Current release.

You won't see the product in the Product Vault until the project is completed. TODO verify whether that's intended.

To move the project between phases, see Move work through phases.

docs.title: The other way: Add product in the Product Vault
docs.text: You can also select Add product in the Product Vault. That creates the product right away with no Workbench project, marked Pending Import, with no release yet. You then upload, process and publish each state yourself. See Create a product.

docs.title: Add the product's documents
docs.text:
Note

This workflow is still being built, so steps and screens may change.

After you start a new product project, add the product's forms to it. A Forms project has a Forms tab only, with no Rates or Rules tabs.

docs.title: Add a form with its file
docs.text:
1. Open the project in Workbench. On the Forms tab, select Create form. The New document dialog opens.
  2. Under Document type, choose Add existing document.
  3. Under Upload Form, select Choose file and pick the form's file (DOC, DOCX or PDF).
  4. Enter a Form Number, then select Use this number to lock it. You see "Form number locked for this form." To pick another number, select Change.
  5. Enter the Edition and the Form Name.
  6. Select Add Form. You see "Successfully added new form", and the form is listed with the change type Addition.

Repeat for each form. To change a form later, select Edit form on its row.

docs.title: Other document types
docs.text:
• New document takes the form's details only, with no file upload (a known limitation). Use Add existing document when you have the file.
  • Bulk import adds many forms at once from an inventory workbook (.xlsx) and a folder of documents. TODO verify the steps; they're covered in a later page.

docs.title: Rates and rules
docs.text:
A project has one type, so rates and rules each need their own project. Start it the same way as your forms project: + New project → New product → the New product card, then choose Rates or Rules under Project type. Rates and rules projects merge into the product's release. They don't create a separate product.

TODO verify what Add existing document asks for in a rates or rules project.

docs.title: Rates project
docs.text:
A rates project uses the Rate Update workflow, with two phases: Select → End. It has a Rates tab.

  1. On the Rates tab, select Create rate. The New document dialog opens.
  2. Under Document type, choose New document or Add existing document.
  3. Under Rate Metadata, enter the Rate Name and Edition.
  4. Select Add Rate. It stays unavailable until both fields are filled in.

docs.title: Rules project
docs.text:
A rules project uses the Rule Update workflow: Select → Review → Approve → End. It has a Rules tab with View package, Edit metadata and Create rule.

  1. On the Rules tab, select Create rule. The New document dialog opens.
  2. Under Document type, choose New document or Add existing document.
  3. Under Rule Metadata, enter the Rule number, Edition and Rule Name.
  4. Select Add Rule.

To set a description and effective date for the rules, select Edit metadata, fill in Description and Effective date, then select Save metadata.

Next: Finish and publish the new product.

docs.title: Finish and publish the new product
docs.text:
Note

This workflow is still being built, so steps and screens may change.

When the product's forms are in, move the project through its phases, then complete it. Completing it as Non-admitted puts the product in the Product Vault with its first release.

docs.title: Move the project to End
docs.text:
1. On the project, select Submit. It appears once the project has a form.
  2. The dialog shows the Current phase and Next phase. Under Select Assignee, choose the person. Add a Due date if you want one, enter your notes under Add notes, then select Submit. You see "Successfully submitted!".
  3. Repeat through Select → Review → Approve → End. From Approve to End, the dialog asks only for notes. A rates project goes straight from Select to End.

From Review on, the person in that phase can also select Reject. See Move work through phases.

docs.title: Complete the project
docs.text:
1. At End, select Complete project.
  2. On the Non-admitted tab, the project's state is already under Destination states. Select Add non-admitted.
  3. Choose the State. Release association is Create new release, and Release version is Baseline.
  4. Pick the New business effective date and Renewal effective date from the calendar, and enter a Description.
  5. Select Preview. It lists the state, "Create new release (Baseline)", and each form with the change New.
  6. Select Complete project. TODO verify what you see right after you confirm.

In the Product Vault, the product's release is Baseline, marked Current release, with your forms on the Forms tab. You don't need Review & publish.

Tip

Pick dates from the calendar. Typed dates may not be saved.

docs.title: If the Admitted tab is empty
docs.text: If the Admitted tab shows "No admitted configurations available.", complete the project as Non-admitted. TODO verify whether admitted configurations can be set up for new products. For filings, see Complete as Admitted.

docs.title: Start a new product project
docs.text:
Note

This workflow is still being built, so steps and screens may change.

Start here when your team is building a brand-new insurance product. The New product wizard has five steps: Product, Project, Configuration, Source and Finalize. Select Next to move on, or Back to change an earlier step.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to Workbench, select + New project, then choose New product ("Create a new insurance product").

  2. Product: under Product type, select the New product card. (The other card, New jurisdiction for existing product, adds a state to a product you already have. See Start a project to add a state.)

  3. Project: under Project type, choose Forms. A project has one type, so rates and rules each need their own project.

  4. Configuration: under Product source type, choose None.

  5. Source: under Product information, enter the Product name and Product description, then choose the Group, Underwriting company, Insurance type, Line of business, Jurisdiction and Type of insurance (for example 19.0 Personal Auto). Subtype of insurance is optional.

  6. Finalize: under Project details, enter the Project title and Project description, and check the Workflow: Product Update for forms, Rate Update for rates or Rule Update for rules. Pick a Due date from the calendar. Project description and Due date are both required. Under Team setup, you're listed in Default members. Add anyone else under Additional members.

  7. Select Create project. The project opens at Select, the first of its phases (Select → Review → Approve → End), with the Forms, Notes, Team and Activity tabs. The Forms tab reads "Add new or existing forms to your project to get started."

Tip

Pick the due date from the calendar, then press Tab to leave the field so the date registers. Typed dates may not be saved.

If Underwriting company shows "No Options" for your group, ask your organization admin to set up the group's underwriting companies. TODO verify where admins set them up.

Next: Add the product's documents.
